title: Rabbit's three chords and key of D; Nash's railroad job in Creston
summary: Nash contrasts himself with Rabbit, who played only C, D and G, mostly in D. The last block then jumps to Nash's job at about 17 on the railroad in Creston, Pennsylvania, after a show stranded him.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Well you weren't like Rabbit, huh? Huh?
You're not like Rabbit, huh? I had three keys. C, D, and G. That's right. C, D, and G. C, D, and G. That's right.
C, D, and G. That's right. Three scales? That's right. Three chords. Three chords as all. That's all he played in, everything he played.
So he could only be playing in that one key, I guess. He'd just be playing in G, I guess, you know?

Well, the most time, I'll tell you, the most time he played in D, D was his favorite key. You see, D would be this chord on the guitar, this. C, and then C, well C, that's right, that's Rabbit keys right here. That would be D, C, and then G. Everything he played right there. Yeah, we got a job there on the railroad. And I worked so hard with such a good worker. I was young. I was around about 17, going to 18. And the fella gave me a job keeping up with the tools, the hammers, the shovels, and whatnot, and all the pigs that they put in the cross ties. You know, when the cross ties would be bad and I'd jam another pig in there and drive a spike in there that'd make it solid. You know, that's what I had to keep up with the spikes, the pigs.
